assumptions: The published terminal product surface is the create-balchemy-agent package exposed as npx balchemy.
The existing Ink cockpit remains the correct foundation for live interactive agent sessions.
Simple inspection, listing, config, doctor, and CI workflows should remain plain CLI commands rather than full-screen TUI flows.
Future validation commands must run in approved container, VPS, or CI contexts because local host pnpm/npm/node/build/test execution is disallowed by project instructions.
This spec is an implementation input; it does not itself authorize production trades, wallet provisioning, key rotation, or deployment actions.

Whether the public CLI roadmap wants separate balchemy auth/config/profile commands or prefers wizard-only onboarding in the short term.
Whether package consumers rely on current exact stdout strings from balchemy list or balchemy docker.
Whether future machine-readable output should be strict JSON only or support NDJSON event streams for long-running commands.
Whether npx execution should keep checking npm registry on every interactive launch or move update checks behind an explicit command.

modernCliPrinciples: Discoverability: every command should have concise help, concrete examples, and typo suggestions.
Consistency: shared global flags, shared output formatting, shared error structure, and predictable stdout/stderr separation.
Composability: read-only commands should be pipe-friendly, deterministic, and support --json for automation.
Safe defaults: prompts must not default to destructive, financial, credential, overwrite, global-install, or production actions.
Human-readable plus machine-readable: default output should be calm and scan-friendly; --json should be stable and schema-backed.
Progressive disclosure: common commands stay short; advanced/internal/debug behavior is reachable but not noisy.
Clear recovery paths: errors explain cause, next command, docs/help hint, and exit code.
Non-interactive readiness: CI must never hang on prompts and must fail closed when required inputs are missing.
modernTuiPrinciples: Keyboard-first navigation with visible shortcut footer and consistent Escape/back/cancel behavior.
Explicit focus state for select, text input, settings edit, and dangerous confirmation surfaces.
Structured panes: header for identity/context, main pane for activity, side/status pane for operational state, overlay for modal actions.
Progressive disclosure: live cockpit shows essentials first and keeps detailed logs/settings behind overlays.
Responsive terminal layout: compact mode below narrow width, robust truncation, no overflow boxes, and predictable wrapping.
Accessible output: no state conveyed by color alone, no mandatory emoji, no-color fallback, copy-paste-friendly text.
Terminal compatibility: TTY checks before alternate screen, no-color and TERM=dumb support, deterministic output in non-TTY/CI.
benchmarksConsidered: GitHub CLI for noun/verb command taxonomy, readable help, --json support, and actionable errors.
Vercel CLI for fast onboarding, project/context clarity, and deployment preview language.
Supabase CLI for local/config/project workflows and CI-friendly command behavior.
Stripe CLI for auth clarity, explicit account context, event/log streaming, and copy-pasteable recovery commands.
Docker CLI for command grouping, inspect/list/log patterns, and machine-readable modes.
Terraform CLI for plan/apply separation, dry-run previews, and destructive confirmation semantics.
Fly.io CLI for concise app context, deploy safety prompts, and remote resource naming clarity.
Linear-style command palette for fast keyboard-driven actions inside a focused TUI.
Charm/Bubble Tea and Ink patterns for terminal layouts, keyboard navigation, and componentized TUI states.
Rich/Textual patterns for tables, panels, progress, and structured error panels.
patternsToAdopt: Use noun-based top-level command groups for durable surfaces: agent, config, auth, context, docker, doctor, tui.
Keep common flows short: balchemy, balchemy init, balchemy start, balchemy list.
Add dry-run/preview to file-writing and execution-adjacent commands: init, docker, future config writes, and risky agent actions.
Separate human stdout, machine stdout, and diagnostics stderr.
Render errors with title, cause, fix, suggested command, docs/help hint, exit code, and debug-only technical details.
Show active agent/context/model/mode in every interactive session header and every risky confirmation.
Use existing create-balchemy-agent/src/tui/text-layout.ts helpers as the terminal width foundation.
Use existing create-balchemy-agent/src/colors.ts behavior for no-color, TERM=dumb, non-TTY, and --no-color.
Create terminal golden tests and JSON schema tests before broad UX refactor.
patternsToAvoid: Do not move CLI/TUI logic into web dashboard or browser frontend surfaces.
Do not make TUI mandatory for simple list/status/config commands.
Do not default yes for updates, overwrites, live execution, production context actions, or credential writes.
Do not print raw secrets, seed phrases, MCP keys, LLM API keys, wallet private keys, or full credential-bearing URLs.
Do not rely on color alone for success, warning, danger, focus, or selection state.
Do not use emoji-only or Unicode-only state symbols without ASCII fallback.
Do not emit spinners, progress redraws, or alternate-screen controls in non-TTY/CI output.
Do not expose hidden/internal MCP tool names as required user knowledge.
Do not add plan/tier/subscription/enterprise CLI concepts.

currentStateAssessment.summary: Balchemy already has a credible terminal foundation: a real npm CLI, an Ink setup wizard, a live cockpit, encrypted local agent storage, color/no-color awareness, width helpers, and trade confirmation. It is not yet a 10/10 CLI/TUI because command taxonomy is shallow, output/error behavior is fragmented, scriptability is weak, file-write/update flows need safer previews, docs drift from implementation, and terminal golden tests are missing.

topProblems.problem: The CLI lacks --json, --quiet, --verbose, --debug, --ci, and --dry-run modes, so automation cannot reliably consume output or avoid prompts.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Balchemy is developer infrastructure; CLI output must work in scripts, CI, agent automation, and incident/debug workflows without brittle text parsing or hanging on prompts.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Add central global option parsing in create-balchemy-agent/src/cli-options.ts and shared reporter behavior in create-balchemy-agent/src/output.ts. Implement JSON mode first for list, version, docker dry-run, config validate/doctor, and future status/current commands.

topProblems.problem: The wizard writes agent.config.yaml and .env, and docker generation writes Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml without a standardized preview, dry-run, or overwrite confirmation contract.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Config and credential-adjacent file writes are high-trust moments. Users need to know exactly what will be created or overwritten, especially in existing project directories and CI.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Introduce a FileWritePreview model used by Wizard and docker-gen: list path, action create/overwrite/append/skip, secret redaction status, and require explicit confirmation unless --dry-run or --ci with non-overwrite-safe behavior.

topProblems.problem: The cockpit shows agent/model/status, but risky execution confirmation should always include agent publicId, endpoint host, mode, chain/token/amount when known, dry-run/shadow/live state, and policy/risk boundary language.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Balchemy separates identity, intent, and execution. The terminal must make the current agent/context/project unmistakable before any live execution path proceeds.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Strengthen TRADE CHECK in App.tsx and ChatAgent.ts to render a structured preview with context, scope, effect, estimated risk, and exact approval text. Require typed confirmation beyond single y for live trades when amount or token is known.

topProblems.problem: Errors are rendered differently across entrypoint, TUI, wizard, config loader, runner, and bridge. Many lack a clear cause/fix/command/exit-code contract.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Auth, config, provider, network, MCP, and execution failures are common in CLI products. A user should recover without reading stack traces or source code.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Create create-balchemy-agent/src/errors.ts and route all terminal-facing errors through a TerminalError structure with code, title, cause, fix, commandSuggestion, docsHint, exitCode, retryable, and debugDetails.

topProblems.problem: README says the wizard handles wallet/chain preferences and behavior rules, while current Wizard.tsx handles provider, key, model, daily cost, and agent setup. Historical TUI specs also differ from current shortcuts and panels.
topProblems.whyItMatters: CLI users often rely on --help and README before running commands. Drift erodes trust and increases setup failure.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Make create-balchemy-agent/README.md and --help reflect actual current behavior, mark historical spec as non-canonical, and add this JSON as the canonical CLI/TUI target contract.

topProblems.problem: docker-gen.ts computes envExampleDest as outDir/.env.example and then passes it as outDir to copyTemplate, likely producing an invalid destination path outDir/.env.example/.env.example.
topProblems.whyItMatters: A setup/deployment command must be boringly reliable. Path bugs damage trust and can block first successful deployment.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Fix copyTemplate call semantics during implementation, then add docker-output tests covering create, skip, dry-run, overwrite, missing dir, and JSON output.

topProblems.problem: The update prompt defaults to yes before running npm install -g balchemy@latest and possibly re-execing the CLI.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Global installs are shared-system mutations. Safe CLI defaults should not turn Enter into a global package update, especially in terminal contexts where users may expect launch continuation.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Default update prompt to no, skip entirely in --ci/non-TTY, and offer explicit balchemy update/check command or a non-blocking hint. Project instructions also state public SDK/CLI must not run periodic self-update loops or background global installs.

topProblems.problem: Existing tests cover helper logic and layout math, but there are no golden/snapshot tests for help/list/docker/error output or full Ink render states.
topProblems.whyItMatters: Terminal UX regressions are easy to miss without golden tests, especially no-color, narrow width, CI, and secret-redaction cases.
topProblems.recommendedFix: Add CLI golden output tests, JSON schema tests, TUI render snapshots, no-color/TERM=dumb tests, overwrite/CI safety tests, and secret redaction tests.

targetExperience.oneSentencePromise: Balchemy CLI should let developers create, inspect, run, and safely supervise AI agents from the terminal with explicit context, predictable commands, scriptable output, and strong execution safeguards.

designPrinciples.principle: Every interactive surface and risky action shows agent, endpoint host, model/provider, mode, and execution state.
Enter must never approve live execution, global installs, overwrites, credential writes, or production context actions by accident.
Read-only and inspection commands have stable --json output and never require a TUI.
Default output is concise, calm, copy-paste-friendly, and structured with clear headings and next commands.
Common tasks stay short and obvious; advanced debugging and raw diagnostics are behind --debug/--verbose/help.
The CLI works in TTY, non-TTY, CI, no-color, TERM=dumb, narrow terminals, and Windows/macOS/Linux terminals.
Tone is precise, direct, security-aware, and developer-friendly; avoid hype, toy-like language, and AI-marketing claims.

shouldAvoid: raw stack traces outside debug mode

targetExperience.cliPersonality: A reliable senior operator: terse by default, explicit before risk, helpful on failure, and stable in automation.
targetExperience.tuiPersonality: A calm command cockpit: keyboard-first, context-rich, low-noise, safety-forward, and optimized for live agent supervision rather than decoration.

globalFlags.behavior: Emit valid JSON to stdout only; diagnostics go to stderr; no ANSI, no spinners, no prompts.
Suppress non-error human output; still emit JSON if --json is also set; never suppress non-zero error messages unless caller redirects stderr.
Show expanded non-secret steps, skipped files/checks, endpoint host, config paths, and timing.
Show technical details and stack traces only after redaction. Never print secrets.
Non-interactive mode: no prompts, no alternate screen, no spinners, deterministic output, fail closed if required input is missing. Implies TERM-safe/no-progress behavior but not --json.
Disable ANSI color; keep text labels and ASCII-safe symbols. Already partially implemented in create-balchemy-agent/src/colors.ts.
Show exact planned actions and file paths without writing files or executing risky actions.

appliesTo: safe file generation only when paired with explicit command and not live execution
globalFlags.behavior: Answer non-dangerous prompts yes. Must not approve trades, wallet mutations, credential deletion, production execution, or global installs.

appliesTo: file overwrite and local store mutation commands
globalFlags.behavior: Allow overwrite/delete only after the command also provides enough explicit target context. Must not bypass live execution confirmation.

commandPatterns.naming: Prefer noun groups for durable surfaces and verbs for actions: agent list/current/use/forget, auth login/logout/status, config list/get/set/validate, docker generate, doctor. Keep short legacy aliases for high-frequency commands.
defaults: No args should remain interactive resume/setup launcher.
Read-only commands should never prompt by default.
File-writing commands should preview creates/overwrites before writing in TTY mode.
CI mode should fail rather than prompt.
Update checks should not block help/version/list/json/ci commands.
Live execution confirmation cannot be bypassed by global --yes.

tuiArchitecture.rationale: Balchemy benefits from TUI for setup, live agent supervision, tool/event review, settings changes, and high-risk confirmation. TUI should not replace plain CLI for list, config validation, auth status, doctor, JSON, or CI usage.

tuiUseCases.whyTui: Provider/model selection, secret entry, daily cost safety cap, and new/existing agent decisions benefit from guided keyboard interaction and progress context.
Long-running agent sessions need status, chat, tool traces, live decisions, and settings in one terminal surface.
Execution previews require focused attention, visible context, and explicit keyboard confirmation.
Provider/model/slippage/strategy changes are session-scoped decisions and should show current values with immediate feedback.

nonTuiUseCases.reason: Should be fast, pipe-friendly, and deterministic.
Diagnostic commands should work in CI and non-TTY.
Preview output must be scriptable and reviewable without alternate screen.
Context inspection should be quick and copy-paste-friendly.
CI must never enter TUI or wait for key input.

primaryActions: Type create to proceed when no overwrites

primaryActions: Type exact confirmation phrase for live execution

navigationModel.primary: Wizard uses linear steps with Escape moving back exactly one valid step. Cockpit uses persistent header/main/status/footer and modal overlays for settings, confirmations, errors, and help.
navigationModel.backCancelBehavior: Esc means back/close/cancel depending on visible overlay. Ctrl+C quits with cleanup. Ctrl+Q quits cockpit. Dangerous overlays treat Esc as cancel, not approve.
navigationModel.focusModel: Only one active input/select at a time. Focused control must be visible by label, position, and text state, not color alone. Modal overlays trap focus until closed or submitted.

shortcutModel.action: Clear visible chat history after local confirmation if unsaved logs would be lost
Return to launcher/switch agent after stopping bridge
Back, close, or cancel; never approve

colors.noColorFallback: Use plain labels and ASCII-safe prefixes. Never rely on color alone. Respect NO_COLOR, TERM=dumb, --no-color, non-TTY stdout, and --ci/no-progress behavior.

tokens.success: green for successful completion or safe live/connected status; fallback label SUCCESS or OK
tokens.warning: gold/yellow for recoverable risk, setup warning, validation warning, or pending review; fallback label WARNING
tokens.danger: red for errors, live execution confirmations, denied actions, and destructive operations; fallback label ERROR or DANGER
tokens.info: cyan/teal for neutral information, provider/model, command hints, and active focus; fallback label INFO
tokens.muted: dim gray for secondary metadata, timestamps, paths, hints, and separators; fallback no prefix or parenthetical text
tokens.accent: teal for Balchemy brand title and selected non-dangerous actions; fallback uppercase BALCHEMY label
tokens.border: gray for neutral panels; yellow for settings/warnings; red for dangerous confirmations; fallback simple ASCII separators
tokens.selected: cyan or inverse text plus leading pointer; fallback '>' pointer
tokens.focus: yellow/cyan label plus control position; fallback explicit Focus: label

layout.maxWidth: Default human output should target 88 columns, wrap at terminal width when available, and remain readable at 80 columns. TUI compact mode starts below 110 columns.
tableRules: Use tables only when rows share the same fields; otherwise use labeled summary blocks.
Do not print full secrets, full API keys, or credential-bearing URLs in tables.
Truncate public IDs and endpoints with middle truncation, preserving host and tail where useful.
In --json mode do not truncate data unless explicitly documented as redacted.
In no-color/non-TTY, preserve markers with ASCII prefixes rather than ANSI color.
panelRules: Use panels for TUI group boundaries only; avoid nested decorative boxes.
Danger confirmations use one prominent red/danger panel and no competing decorative elements.
Settings overlays use yellow/warning border; errors use red/danger; neutral status uses gray.
Panels must degrade to simple headings and separators in non-TTY/plain CLI output.
spacingRules: One blank line before major sections in plain CLI output, none after final line unless readability requires it.
Keep command suggestions copy-pasteable on their own line.
Avoid multi-paragraph terminal blocks; prefer title/cause/fix/command rows.
wrappingRules: Use text-layout.ts displayWidth, truncateEnd, truncateMiddle, and wrapText for terminal-visible strings.
Never split secrets across lines; redact before wrapping.
Long JSON-like tool payloads in TUI should collapse to a short summary with debug expansion only.
At widths below 80, prioritize context, error title, and next command over decorative labels.

rules: Header must fit 80 columns by truncating model/publicId with truncateMiddle.
Never show full API key or bearer token in header.
Live mode must be visible as text, not only green color.

requiredFields: back/cancel hint when overlay is active
rules: Footer shortcut line must reflect current mode and width.
Danger overlay footer must mention Esc cancels.
Selection must be clear without color.
Use concise labels; explain risk/cost in secondary text.
Tables must have stable columns in human mode and stable keys in JSON mode.
Avoid truncating in JSON mode except redaction.
Lists show active/current marker where applicable.
Empty states include the next command.
Use label/value rows.
Group security-sensitive fields under a redacted credentials section.
Validation errors keep focus in the field.
Secret fields use SecretInput, never TextInput.
Defaults are shown but not silently applied when invalid input is entered.
Dangerous actions require typed confirmation, not Enter default.
Show exact target and effect.
Esc and blank input cancel.
--yes cannot approve live trades or wallet/key mutations.
Use inline status in TUI.
Use one-line step messages in plain CLI.
Suppress spinners in non-TTY/CI/JSON/quiet.
Every long-running step should have a terminal success or failure line.
No raw stack traces unless --debug.
No secrets in technical details.
Use consistent exit codes from errorStandards.
Say what is empty, why it may be empty, and the next command.
Example: 'No saved agents. Run balchemy init to create one or balchemy auth login to connect existing credentials.'
Show only mode-relevant shortcuts first.
Keep full shortcut list under ? overlay and README.
Shortcuts in code, --help, and README must match.

defaultHumanReadable.stdout: Primary command result, summaries, tables, success messages, and next-step commands.
defaultHumanReadable.stderr: Warnings, errors, update notices, debug diagnostics, and progress for long-running non-JSON commands when stdout may be piped.
rules: No ANSI when color disabled or stdout is not TTY.
No secrets or full API keys.
No spinner redraw in non-TTY.
No markdown tables in terminal output; use padded rows or plain lists.

jsonMode.stdout: Only valid JSON, no ANSI, no headings, no trailing logs, no spinners.
jsonMode.stderr: Non-JSON warnings/errors only when necessary; keep machine stdout clean.
rules: JSON mode never enters TUI.
JSON mode never prompts; if input is missing, return ok=false with error and non-zero exit.
Secret values are redacted as '[redacted]' and include redacted=true metadata where useful.
For long-running future watch/log modes, prefer NDJSON only if a distinct --ndjson flag is introduced.

quietMode.behavior: Suppress non-essential success/info output. Keep errors on stderr and JSON stdout when --json is present.
rules: Do not suppress prompts in interactive TTY unless --ci is also set; instead avoid using quiet for prompt-heavy flows.
Do not hide destructive confirmation text.

verboseMode.behavior: Show expanded steps, file paths, skipped actions, config source, endpoint host, provider/model, and check timing without stack traces.
rules: Never print secret values.
Use stderr for diagnostic progress if stdout may be machine-consumed.

debugMode.behavior: Show redacted stack traces, request ids, HTTP status codes, provider endpoint host, retry attempts, and raw error class names.
rules: Apply redaction before rendering.
Never print MCP API keys, LLM API keys, Authorization headers, seed phrases, private keys, DSNs, or full credential-bearing URLs.
Debug mode does not bypass safety confirmations.

ciMode.behavior: Non-interactive deterministic command behavior. No alternate screen, no prompts, no browser opening, no update prompt, no spinner animation.
rules: Fail with exit code 2 for missing required input or command misuse.
Fail with exit code 4 for unsafe operation requiring confirmation unless --dry-run is used or explicit safe flags are provided.
CI mode should be compatible with --json.

dryRunMode.behavior: Show planned file writes, overwrites, config mutations, or execution-adjacent actions without applying them.
rules: Dry-run output includes exact paths and create/overwrite/append/skip actions.
Dry-run JSON includes plan array with action, path, exists, wouldOverwrite, containsSecret, and redactedPreview where safe.

error.title: Missing environment variable
error.cause: agent.config.yaml references LLM_API_KEY but it is not set.
error.fix: Add LLM_API_KEY to .env next to the config file or export it before running balchemy start.

structure.title: Short human-readable error title, e.g. Missing config file
structure.cause: One sentence explaining what failed and which file/command/context was involved.
structure.fix: One concrete next step the user can take.
structure.commandSuggestion: A copy-pasteable command when applicable, e.g. balchemy config validate agent.config.yaml --verbose
structure.docsHint: Use command-local help first, e.g. Run balchemy start --help. External docs link only when already documented and stable.
structure.exitCode: Numeric exit code from the standard map.
structure.debugDetails: Only in --debug; redacted stack, status code, request id, endpoint host, and retry info.

exitCodeMap.meaning: File system write/read permission or conflict

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Unknown command: statr
Did you mean balchemy start?
Run balchemy --help for available commands.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Use typo suggestion when edit distance <= 2; otherwise show top-level command list.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Missing config file
Cause: agent.config.yaml was not found in the current directory.
Fix: Run balchemy init or pass a config path.
Command: balchemy start ./agent.config.yaml
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Suggest balchemy init for new users and balchemy config validate <path> for existing configs.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Missing environment variable
Cause: agent.config.yaml references LLM_API_KEY but it is not set.
Fix: Add LLM_API_KEY to .env next to the config file or export it before running start.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Show the missing variable name, never the secret value.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Invalid YAML config
Cause: agent.config.yaml could not be parsed.
Fix: Check indentation and run balchemy config validate agent.config.yaml --verbose.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: In --debug include parser line/column if available.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Provider key rejected
Cause: Anthropic returned 401/403 while validating the key.
Fix: Paste a valid provider API key or choose another provider.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Keep focus in SecretInput; do not print key.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Balchemy API key rejected
Cause: The MCP endpoint returned 401 for the active agent key.
Fix: Check the saved agent credentials or run balchemy auth login.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Show publicId and endpoint host; redact key.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Network request timed out
Cause: The CLI could not reach api.balchemy.ai within 8 seconds.
Fix: Check network access and retry.
Command: balchemy doctor --verbose
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Mark retryable=true and include endpoint host in debug details.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Overwrite confirmation required
Cause: ./agent.config.yaml already exists.
Fix: Review the preview and type overwrite, or rerun with --dry-run to inspect without writing.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Never overwrite by default. In --ci fail closed unless --force is explicitly provided for file commands.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Cannot write file
Cause: Permission denied while writing ./deploy/Dockerfile.
Fix: Choose a writable directory or adjust permissions.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Show path; avoid stack trace unless --debug.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Trade confirmation required
Cause: The external LLM requested trade_command for the active live agent.
Fix: Review token, amount, chain, mode, and type the exact confirmation phrase to proceed.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: In TUI, keep confirmation overlay focused; in non-TUI, refuse unless an authorized non-interactive execution flow is explicitly designed.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Trade cancelled
Cause: User rejected the TRADE CHECK prompt.
Fix: No action was executed. Send a new instruction if you want a different trade preview.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Record cancellation in activity as system/tool result, not as error.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Execution denied by policy
Cause: Behavior rules or pre-trade risk checks blocked the requested action.
Fix: Review active rules and risk output before trying another instruction.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Show denial reason and related rule/check id when available.

errorTypes.exampleMessage:
Non-interactive input required
Cause: This command needs a prompt, but --ci was used.
Fix: Provide required flags or run interactively.

Interactive terminal required
Cause: The cockpit needs a TTY, but stdout is not interactive.
Fix: Run balchemy start in a terminal, or use balchemy config validate --json for CI checks.
errorTypes.recoverySuggestion: Do not emit alternate-screen escape codes in non-TTY.

dangerousOperations.risk: Financial execution through authorized backend/trading layer.
dangerousOperations.requiredUx: TRADE CHECK overlay with exact action, amount, token, chain when known, publicId, endpoint host, mode, policy/risk notes, and typed confirmation.

dangerousOperations.risk: Overwriting local config or secret files.
dangerousOperations.requiredUx: File preview table and explicit create/overwrite confirmation; dry-run support.

dangerousOperations.risk: Overwriting deployment files and misdirecting setup.
dangerousOperations.requiredUx: Dry-run preview, overwrite detection, --force semantics, and tests for .env.example path.

dangerousOperations.risk: Mutates global npm installation and can alter shared machine state.
dangerousOperations.requiredUx: Default no, skip in CI/non-TTY/help/version/json, and prefer explicit update command.

dangerousOperations.risk: Removes local encrypted credential references and active context.
dangerousOperations.requiredUx: Show publicId and endpoint host; require typed publicId or 'forget <short-id>' confirmation; never delete without explicit target.
Masked input, provider label, reconnection status, rollback hint, and no raw key in activity.

requiresConfirmation.confirmation: For live known-amount trades, require typed phrase 'execute <action> <amount> <symbol-or-token-tail>' or an equivalent exact phrase. Single y is acceptable only for shadow/dry-run or incomplete non-executing previews.
Require typing 'overwrite' in TTY or passing --force for file commands; --yes alone is not enough for overwrites.
Require 'create' in TTY when .env will be written; show that secrets will be stored locally and .env will be added to .gitignore.
Default to no and require explicit y/yes; never run in --ci; consider moving to balchemy update.
Require typed publicId or exact short id.
Show production endpoint/context and require typed 'production' only for actions that are explicitly authorized and safe in CLI scope.

supportsDryRun.behavior: Run wizard until file/action preview, then show planned local writes and onboarding requirements without writing files or saving agent credentials.
Show planned Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml/.env.example create/overwrite/skip actions without writing.
Show planned config file mutation and validation result without writing.
Preview request/context/policy checks without submitting live execution.

allowedFor: safe prompt continuation in CI when all inputs are explicit
overwriting local generated files after explicit command target
forgetting local saved agent after explicit publicId target

productionContextWarnings: Always show endpoint host and publicId in live cockpit header.
If endpoint host is api.balchemy.ai or config mode is live, label mode as LIVE in text.
For any future production-affecting CLI command, require explicit typed production confirmation and never default yes.
Do not expose production credentials, raw bearer tokens, or wallet keys in terminal output, debug logs, JSON, or screenshots.

rollbackGuidance.guidance: Before overwrite, show backup path or recommend copying existing file; future implementation may create .bak only with explicit confirmation.
Show previous provider/model in activity and suggest reverting via Ctrl+S settings if reconnect fails.
Dry-run first; if overwritten, show exact files changed and suggest git diff for tracked files.
State that no action was executed; for denied trades, show risk/policy reason and suggest adjusting instruction rather than bypassing checks.

firstRunFlow.targetBehavior: If agents exist, show active/most recent context with actions resume, choose, new. If none, launch wizard. In --ci, do not prompt; return error with suggested command.
Show provider choices and explain external LLM powers decisions while Balchemy enforces scoped execution.
Use SecretInput, validate when possible, never print key, and explain storage destination before writing .env/encrypted store.
Cost cap validation must reject invalid values instead of silently defaulting to 5.
Explain walletless onboarding vs existing endpoint; show publicId and endpoint host after success.
Show file plan for agent.config.yaml, .env, .gitignore, and encrypted store before writing.
Start cockpit with explicit agent/model/mode header and initial empty-state guidance.

loginFlow.targetBehavior: Interactive TTY: choose create new walletless agent or connect existing MCP endpoint/API key. Non-TTY/CI: require endpoint and key via env/flags and never prompt.
Validate endpoint shape, read key from env, save encrypted store only if explicitly allowed, and emit JSON summary when --json is set.

logoutFlow.targetBehavior: Clear active agent selection only; do not delete saved credentials unless --forget or agent forget is explicitly used.
Delete saved local agent after typed publicId confirmation or explicit --force with exact publicId in CI.

authConfigUx.currentContextDisplay: Every context display should include active publicId, endpoint host, provider, model, mode live/shadow/setup, config source, credential storage state encrypted/plaintext-migrated, and createdAt. It must never include raw API keys, bearer tokens, private keys, seed phrases, or full credential-bearing URLs.

configCommands.purpose: Check file existence, YAML parse, env substitutions, required fields, provider normalization, and safe defaults without launching TUI.
Print effective non-secret config with redacted secret fields and config/env source information.
Read one non-secret effective value; secret keys return redacted metadata, not secret value.
Safely mutate supported local config keys with validation, preview, and confirmation.

authConfigUx.ciAuthMode: CI auth must use environment variables or explicit non-secret references only. Recommended inputs: MCP_ENDPOINT, BALCHEMY_API_KEY, LLM_API_KEY, and optional BALCHEMY_AGENT_PUBLIC_ID. CI commands must not open browser, enter alternate screen, prompt for input, or write credentials unless explicitly requested with safe flags.
tokenHandlingRules: Read secrets from env or SecretInput only.
Write secrets only to .env or encrypted agent store after preview/confirmation.
Append .env to .gitignore when writing .env, but preview the append action first.
Redact secrets in human output, JSON output, debug output, TUI activity, tests, and errors.
Mask provider keys using fixed head/tail only when necessary; prefer '[redacted]' for machine output.
Never print Authorization headers, raw MCP API keys, LLM API keys, wallet private keys, seed phrases, DSNs, or credential-bearing URLs.
Do not leak backend business logic, trading internals, privileged operational workflows, or private endpoints into the public CLI.

mustPass: All existing commands continue to work: balchemy, init, start, list, docker, --help, --version, --no-color.
No CLI/TUI work touches balchemy-frontend-v2, browser pages, dashboard components, landing page, or marketing components.
--json output for supported commands parses as valid JSON and contains no ANSI escapes.
--ci never enters TUI, opens browser, shows spinner animation, prompts, or performs global update prompts.
NO_COLOR=1, TERM=dumb, --no-color, and non-TTY output contain no ANSI escapes.
No terminal output includes raw MCP API keys, LLM API keys, bearer tokens, private keys, seed phrases, DSNs, or credential-bearing URLs.
Trade confirmation cannot be approved accidentally with blank Enter and cannot be bypassed by --yes.
Wizard file writes and docker generation show dry-run/preview and require confirmation for overwrites.
Errors render title/cause/fix/command/help/exit code and stack traces appear only in --debug with redaction.
Help, README, and TUI shortcut footer agree on command names and keyboard shortcuts.
manualQa: Run first-run setup in a TTY with no saved agents and confirm wizard sequence, secret masking, cost validation, file preview, and cockpit launch.
Run default balchemy with saved agents and confirm resume/list/new choices are clear and no accidental setup occurs.
Run cockpit at 80, 100, 109, 110, 124, and 148 columns and confirm no overflow, clipped borders, or hidden confirmation text.
Trigger provider auth failure and network timeout and confirm recovery messages are actionable.
Trigger TRADE CHECK with sample trade args and confirm context/action/amount/mode are visible and cancel path records no execution.
Run docker generation against a directory with existing Dockerfile/docker-compose.yml/.env.example and confirm preview/overwrite behavior.
Check copy-paste ergonomics of suggested commands in errors and next-step output.
Check Windows/macOS/Linux terminal behavior in approved environments or CI matrices where available.
terminalCompatibilityChecks: NO_COLOR=1 balchemy --help has no ANSI escapes.
TERM=dumb balchemy list has no ANSI escapes and no Unicode-only state dependency.
balchemy list --json stdout parses as JSON and stderr is empty for success.
balchemy doctor --ci --json never prompts and exits non-zero on missing required inputs.
Non-TTY balchemy start refuses TUI with TERMINAL_UNSUPPORTED_TUI rather than emitting alternate-screen escapes.
Narrow terminal render tests cover 80-column and below-110 compact layout.
Secret redaction tests cover human, JSON, verbose, debug, and TUI activity paths.

finalReviewChecklist: Scope is CLI/TUI-only and contains no web UI/dashboard/browser frontend/landing page/marketing component recommendations.
Every changed command has human output, JSON behavior where applicable, exit code, and CI behavior defined.
Every dangerous operation has a preview/confirmation/cancel path and a statement about --yes/--force limits.
All terminal output paths use shared reporter/error/redaction utilities rather than ad hoc process.stdout/process.stderr writes where practical.
Secrets are redacted before rendering or logging, including debug mode and tests.
TUI screens show agent/context/mode before risky actions.
No state depends only on color; no-color and TERM=dumb remain readable.
Non-TTY and --ci do not enter alternate screen or prompt.
README, --help, TUI footer, and tests agree on shortcuts and command names.
Historical docs are updated or marked non-canonical to prevent spec drift.
Docker generation .env.example path behavior is tested.
Local host validation restrictions are respected; builds/tests/typechecks run only in approved container/VPS/CI contexts.
doNotDo: Do not touch browser frontend pages.
Do not touch landing page implementation.
Do not edit balchemy-frontend-v2 for this CLI/TUI work.
Do not introduce plan/tier/subscription/enterprise CLI concepts.
Do not add transactional email infrastructure or email setup flows.
Do not leak backend business logic, trading internals, private endpoints, or privileged operational workflows into the public CLI.
Do not expose raw secrets, private keys, seed phrases, DSNs, tokens, bearer headers, or credential-bearing URLs in terminal output.
Do not perform real trades, wallet provisioning, approvals, withdrawals, key rotation, or wallet mutations as part of CLI/TUI UX implementation.
Do not let --yes or --force bypass live trade confirmation, policy checks, risk checks, or wallet/key safety boundaries.
Do not default prompts to yes for global installs, overwrites, live execution, production actions, credential deletion, or wallet/key operations.
Do not emit alternate-screen escape sequences outside an interactive TTY.
Do not rely on color, emoji, or Unicode-only symbols as the sole carrier of meaning.
Do not print raw stack traces outside --debug, and even debug output must be redacted.
Do not run local host pnpm/npm/node/build/typecheck/test commands for this repository; use approved container/VPS/CI contexts.
